articles.title: Leicestershire facing relegation over pitch penalty, and more: County Championship cricket, day three – live
articles.summary: All the latest updates from around the grounds. Middlesex chair Sykes to resign | Email Tanya. It was advantage Warwickshire at the top but perhaps the most significant action of the day came off the pitch and at the bottom, with Leicestershire all but relegated after a points deduction.
body: The Cricket Regulator had charged Leicestershire after the Grace Road pitch was rated as poor for last month’s win against Glamorgan. The cricket discipline panel has upheld the charge, leading to the deduction of the 19 points picked up for the victory plus eight more as a penalty. A Leicestershire statement said “the club is reviewing its position and considering all available options”, but the deduction left them bottom of the table, 38 points adrift of the last safe spot. With Hampshire 225 ahead with seven wickets standing, Leicestershire’s hopes in what is now a must-win match are slim.

Warwickshire flourish a 19-point hand on the table and wait after a second two-day victory in succession. Essex, further weakened by overnight substitutions to Shane Snater and Tom Westley, gave them the upper hand by conceding another 40 runs for the last wicket, thanks largely to an unbeaten 88 from Sam Hain. The Indian spinner Manav Suthar, with five for 75, and Chris Woakes, with three for 33, were too hot for Essex and Warwickshire easily knocked off the 133 needed.

articles.title: ‘It is for every fan who has ever followed us’: Bournemouth’s European debut caps journey from the brink
articles.summary: Club legend Steve Fletcher reflects on the wild rise over two decades to playing Real Sociedad in the Europa League. It is 13 years since Bournemouth, a couple of months after finishing runners-up to Doncaster in the third tier, hosted Real Madrid.
body: An early, wayward Ronaldo free-kick broke the wrist of an 11-year‑old boy before Madrid ran out 6-0 winners in a bucket-list friendly.

“I retired a month earlier, and I thought: ‘Yeah, that’s typical, isn’t it?’” says Steve Fletcher, a bona fide Bournemouth legend and now club ambassador who scored 121 goals across 728 appearances, a smile unravelling on his face. “You play for a club for 20 years, and then you go and get the biggest team in the world to come down. I wanted to say to Eddie Howe: ‘Can I have five minutes on the pitch?’ For them to play here was utterly ridiculous.”

It was one of the stranger days in Bournemouth’s recent history and on Thursday they will take another step when they face Real Sociedad in their first competitive game against European opposition. On the final day of last season, Bournemouth’s staff and players celebrated qualifying for the Europa League by gathering around a “Rayanair” flag depicting their Brazil forward piloting a plane, giddy supporters providing the perfect backdrop for the pictures, and those fans have since booked trips to Prague, Oslo and Vigo.

articles.title: How an Aston Villa fringe player became Europe's most prolific scorer
articles.summary: No player in Europe's top five leagues has scored more goals than Donyell Malen since his Roma debut in January - BBC Sport examines his transformation.
body: Just eight months ago, Donyell Malen was struggling to make a significant impact at Aston Villa.
Today, no player in Europe's top five leagues has scored more goals since his Roma debut on 18 January.

The Netherlands international has enjoyed a remarkable turnaround since joining Roma, transforming from a player who struggled to establish himself in the Premier League into one of the continent's most productive forwards.
Since his Roma debut, Malen has scored 20 goals, more than Harry Kane (16), Lamine Yamal (15) and anyone else in the Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1 during the same period.

articles.title: Brian Dubiski: ‘Everything I do is about Madison. It’s a big reason I did this game at Wembley’
articles.summary: Man behind US college football’s landmark match in London has dedicated his life to improving crowd safety since his daughter was killed in a crowd crush at a concert aged 23.
body: O n Saturday afternoon, as he looks out at the crowd of 60,000 he has helped entice to Wembley Stadium, Brian Dubiski’s dream will become a reality. But, as Arizona State and Kansas make history by playing the first US college football game in Britain, Dubiski will think most of his daughter, Madison, who was crushed to death at the age of 23.

Madison and nine other people were trampled and suffocated by a crowd at a Travis Scott concert in Houston in November 2021. Dubiski now dedicates his life to keeping people safe at sporting events and concerts and, since December, Wembley is one of the stadiums that follows the protocols he introduced.

As the chairman, CEO and co-founder of Union Jack Classic, which has planned and organised Saturday’s game, Dubiski will sit in the Royal Box at Wembley. His memories of Madison will also be sparked by the sight of the cheerleaders for both teams – for his daughter also used to be a cheerleader.

articles.title: Rancour, road trips and revival: tale of battle for Brighton’s future hits the stage
articles.summary: New play spotlights fans’ tortuous trek from the Goldstone Ground, via Gillingham and an athletics stadium. It was the tip-off that changed Ian Hart’s life for ever. The funeral director from Worthing was co-editor of the Brighton fanzine Gull’s Eye when he received a phone call from Gordon…
body: “Gordon always wanted to join the Brighton board, but they didn’t want him there,” Hart says. “Ron Noades [the Palace chair] welcomed him with open arms. One of his [Lucking’s] employees had been on this golf day and someone got pissed in the evening and said: ‘You’ll never guess what’s happened – Brighton have sold the Goldstone Ground and are moving to Portsmouth.’ Gordon loved it, because it was another nail in Brighton’s coffin.”

Hart initially struggled to believe that Brighton’s home since 1902 could be in danger, but decided to confront the chief executive, David Bellotti, at his office. “I parked the hearse outside, went in and asked him straight whether they had sold the ground and were moving to Portsmouth,” Hart writes in his book, Brighton & Hove Albion: From Every Angle, which was released last year. “All the colour drained from his face.”

articles.title: Chelsea's Lavia out to 'change narrative' after injuries
articles.summary: Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia says he is finally reaping the rewards of his hard work and is determined to "change the narrative" around him.
body: Now 22, the Belgian is on the verge of enjoying his longest spell in the Chelsea side and, if he completes 60 minutes against Brentford on Friday, will surpass his previous best run of 518 minutes without injury - including pre-season matches.
Such progress has been some time in the making. Lavia made only one appearance in his first season at Chelsea because of a serious hamstring injury.

In his second campaign, he suffered a series of setbacks and missed 33 games, down from 42 the previous season, before significantly improving his availability last term by featuring in about half of Chelsea 's matches.
He has now remained available throughout pre-season and the opening weeks of the new campaign.

articles.title: Do Celtic have 'big issues', or will next four days hush concerns?
articles.summary: Chris Sutton believes his former side have "great concerns" despite a winning start to the Scottish Premiership season. The next four days will tell us whether those worries are justified.
body: Football in Glasgow's goldfish bowl has a habit of being unnecessarily dramatised, yet there is a case for saying a week in mid-September could have a defining impact on Celtic's season.
After spectacularly failing the first of three tests during this mini crucial spell, alarm bells are ringing among sections of an unconvinced support.

Martin O'Neill's side have the chance to right the wrongs of their sobering 3-0 Premier Sports Cup quarter-final defeat by Rangers at Ibrox when they host their city rivals in a rematch in the league on Sunday, but a Europa League opener with Ferencvaros comes first.

Celtic fans are tiptoeing with trepidation into their first European action since their Champions League play-off collapse in Linz, a capitulation that has the same supporters questioning this team's big-game credentials, especially after Sunday.

articles.title: Klopp makes decision on Germany's new first-choice goalkeeper: "A team needs stability and a spine"
articles.summary: After coming out of international retirement to play for Germany at the World Cup, Manuel Neuer has now definitively retired from international football. As a result, new Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has had to identify a new first-choice goalkeeper, and his decision has fallen on Marc-André ter…
body: "Yes, for the moment, there is one, Marc-André ter Stegen," Klopp confirmed when asked if he has a first-choice goalkeeper.

"A team needs stability and a spine, and then you can add a lot of youth around that. I've known him for ages. Manuel Neuer was the best goalkeeper in the world for a long time. Nevertheless, everyone knew that ter Stegen was world-class too. He then suffered an injury at an unfortunate time. At the moment, he is fit and the same goalkeeper he was before. He brings experience with him. He is making a very good impression. Everything depends on performance."
Klopp named a total of 44 players, split into two squads, for the upcoming four UEFA Nations League games.
In terms of the goalkeepers, Finn Dahmen ( Augsburg ), Alexander Nübel (Besiktas) and Marc-André ter Stegen (Ajax) have been included in the squad for the first two games.

articles.title: Tottenham Hotspur set for huge injury boost ahead of Aston Villa clash
articles.summary: Pedro Porro Boost Gives Tottenham Options Ahead of Aston Villa Clash. Tottenham have some good news at last. Pedro Porro is available again for the visit of Aston Villa, after missing the last two matches with a “muscular issue”.
body: Roberto De Zerbi confirmed the Spain international will be ready for Saturday’s lunchtime fixture in north London. After the 3-1 Carabao Cup defeat at Liverpool, he kept the message simple. Spurs have not clicked yet, but he clearly believes they will.
“I believe in my players, I have a big confidence, a big opinion of my players, and when we arrive to find the click, to win a game, I think we enjoy with these players.”

Porro’s comeback gives Tottenham more balance and more thrust. He is one of those full-backs who plays like an extra winger, which suits De Zerbi’s approach. That matters even more when the team is struggling for goals and rhythm.

Spurs also welcomed Mohammed Kudus back into the starting line-up at Anfield. It was his first Tottenham start since the long-term quad injury he suffered in January, and De Zerbi made it clear he sees him as central to the attack.

articles.title: IRFU await news of 'massive opportunity' to join PWR
articles.summary: Lynne Cantwell, Irish Rugby's head of women's strategy, believes the possibility of teams from Ireland forming part of a future British and Irish League represents "a massive opportunity".
body: Premiership Women's Rugby [PWR], currently restricted to English clubs, opened an expression of interest process in April for organisations who might join the nine-team competition if it expanded, with the Irish Rugby Football Union confirming at the time that they had shown interest in joining.
A decision about whether the Irish Rugby Football Union [IRFU], and its Scottish and Welsh counterparts, have been successful in a bid to join PWR is expected within the next three to four months.
Cantwell told Irish broadcaster RTE that the prospect of a potential merger between PWR and the Celtic Challenge, presently contested by Irish, Scottish and Welsh sides, is an exciting one.
"I think the opportunity is incredibly massive, when we look at the elite competition that we want our national players and emerging players to be part of," she said.

articles.summary: Germany coach Jurgen Klopp handed 16 players their first call-ups on Thursday as he unveiled a 44-man squad for his first camp since taking over as coach in the summer.
body: Teams are restricted to naming 20 outfield players and three goalkeepers for each match but the former Liverpool manager took the unusual step of naming a larger squad.
Klopp has split the group into two separate squads for Germany's four upcoming Nations League fixtures.
The first group will be available for the games fixtures against the Netherlands in Amsterdam on September 24 and at home to Greece three days later in Augsburg.
The second group will be available for Germany's matches against Serbia in Munich on October 1 and Greece in Thessaloniki on October 4.

articles.title: 'More risk earlier!' - Norris braces for 'tougher' Monaco with shock Sprint
articles.summary: World champion Lando Norris believes Formula 1 drivers will face a greater challenge at next year's Monaco Grand Prix than normal due to the addition of the Sprint format.
body: The 24-round 2027 calendar, published on Wednesday, includes 10 Sprint weekends - four more than this season - with Monaco's street circuit to host the alternative format for the first time.

The Principaliy's narrow track is not known for overtaking, where the Sprint format has hitherto tended to be used, but is considered arguably the greatest challenge in the sport for an F1 driver when it comes to qualifying.

Reacting to the news when speaking with Sky Sports F1's Natalie Pinkham alongside golfer Justin Rose during an appearance at the BMW PGA Championship Pro-Am at Wentworth on Wednesday, McLaren's Norris said: "Interesting!
"I guess the main thing is that means you've got FP1, [Sprint] qualifying on Friday - which is the challenge.
